classification.difficultyReason: Infer equal angles from the two perpendicular pairs and equal distances from the square’s centre to prove congruence, then replace equal triangular areas to identify the overlap as a quarter-square. The construction, triangle pair and target area equality are supplied.

content.prompt: A 3-metre square and a 4-metre square overlap as shown in the diagram. $D$ is the centre of the 3-metre square.

spec.description: Upright square A B F C and tilted square with vertex D. The overlap DEFG has a light blue fill replacing the source grey. X, Y and perpendiculars are absent from the question diagram. The chosen tilt is illustrative, not a numerical given.
spec.mathematics: AC = 3 m; tilted square side = 4 m; D is the centre of ABFC; E lies on CF and the tilted side through D; G lies on BF and the perpendicular tilted side through D.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, labels, the centre point and the requested shaded region are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw the interval $DY$ where $Y$ is on $GF$ and $DY\perp GF$. Draw the interval $DX$ where $X$ is on $CF$ and $DX\perp CF$.

answer.short: Draw $DY$ horizontally from $D$ to $GF$, and $DX$ vertically from $D$ to $CF$.
answer.worked: Place $Y$ directly to the right of $D$ on $GF$, and $X$ directly below $D$ on $CF$. Join $D$ to $Y$ and $D$ to $X$, marking the right angles at $Y$ and $X$.

spec.description: Complete supplied figure with dashed DX and DY, labels X and Y and right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: X is the midpoint of CF, Y is the midpoint of BF, DX is perpendicular to CF and DY is perpendicular to GF.
spec.answerVisibility: The requested construction is visible only in the solution.

answer.short: $\triangle DXE\equiv\triangle DYG$ by two equal angles and the corresponding equal side $DX=DY$.
answer.worked: Since $D$ is the centre of the 3-metre square, $DX=DY=\frac32\text{ m}$. Also $\angle DXE=\angle DYG=90^\circ$. The sides $DE$ and $DG$ are perpendicular, as are $DX$ and $DY$, so $\angle XDE=\angle YDG$. Therefore $\triangle DXE\equiv\triangle DYG$ by the two-angle-and-side test (AAS).

answer.short: Replace $\triangle DYG$ by its congruent triangle $\triangle DXE$; the remaining region $DEFY$ is common.
answer.worked:
Congruent triangles have equal areas. Thus
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(DEFG)&=\operatorname{area}(DEFY)+\operatorname{area}(\triangle DYG)\\\operatorname{area}(DEFG)&=\operatorname{area}(DEFY)+\operatorname{area}(\triangle DXE)\\\operatorname{area}(DEFG)&=\operatorname{area}(DXFY).\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the area of the shaded region.

answer.short:
$\frac94\text{ m}^2$.

The overlap has the same area as the quarter-square $DXFY$.
answer.worked:
$DXFY$ is a square with side $\frac32\text{ m}$, since $D$ is the centre of the 3-metre square. By part c,
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(DEFG)&=\operatorname{area}(DXFY)\\\operatorname{area}(DEFG)&=\frac32\times\frac32\\\operatorname{area}(DEFG)&=\frac94\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
